ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a schematic diagram of the water balance of a certain drainage basin. At the top there is “precipitation 925.92”; at the upper left there is “evaporation 254.11”; in the middle there is “river channel runoff 631.81”; on the right side there is a box labeled “Jia 40.00”; “Jia” receives an arrow indicating the direction of water quantity from above, and is connected with the groundwater part below where “extraction of groundwater X” is located. Then reason: What Jia represents is not evaporation, nor river channel runoff or incoming runoff, but the process by which precipitation or surface water transfers to groundwater. In the water cycle links, this process is called “infiltration.”
